title: SceneMultiplayer.get_authenticating_peers() still returns peer IDs after both sides have successfully called complete_auth()
body:
### Tested versions

v4.7.1.stable.mono.official [a13da4feb]

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1062) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11800H @ 2.30GHz (16 threads) - 23.74 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Even after both the server and the client have correctly called `SceneMultiplayer.complete_auth(id)`, the server-side `get_authenticating_peers()` continues to include that client ID for a noticeable period of time.

This causes serious problems in practice:
1. Code that checks `get_authenticating_peers()` and then calls `complete_auth()` will hit the peer again.
2. Calling `complete_auth()` repeatedly for the same ID will cause an error in C++.

```
E 0:00:08:874   NativeCalls.cs:737 @ int Godot.NativeCalls.godot_icall_1_85(nint, nint, int): The authentication session was already marked as completed.
  <C++ Error>   Condition "pending_peers[p_peer].local" is true. Returning: ERR_FILE_CANT_WRITE
  <C++ Source>  modules/multiplayer/scene_multiplayer.cpp:481 @ complete_auth()
  <Stack Trace> NativeCalls.cs:737 @ int Godot.NativeCalls.godot_icall_1_85(nint, nint, int)
                SceneMultiplayer.cs:247 @ Godot.Error Godot.SceneMultiplayer.CompleteAuth(int)
                Lobby.cs:136 @ void Lobby.AuthCallback(long, System.Byte[])
                Callable.generics.cs:75 @ void Godot.Callable.<From>g__Trampoline|3_0<T0, T1>(object, Godot.NativeInterop.NativeVariantPtrArgs, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant&)
                DelegateUtils.cs:86 @ void Godot.DelegateUtils.InvokeWithVariantArgs(nint, System.Void*, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant**, int, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant*)
```

Since this error can be detected at the C++ level, why doesn't `get_authenticating_peers` return the correct list of IDs? Is this the expected behavior?


### The solution I want:

Once both peers have called `complete_auth()`, the corresponding ID should no longer appear in `get_authenticating_peers()` (or at least the local side should be able to know that it has already completed authentication and avoid the error).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Set up a simple server + client with auth_callback enabled.
2. On both sides, call complete_auth(peer_id) when authentication succeeds.
3. Immediately (or in the next few frames) print multiplayer.get_authenticating_peers() on the server.
4. Observe that the client ID is still present.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
